=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:543 (job `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The required CI job `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` fails on PR head 66fe05bf631890d9b00ee2c2af9af527272ad551, so the aggregate `lint` job (line 3466) fails with "CI jobs that did not succeed: tests-hooks-and-orchestrator", and the available log tail does not show which step or assertion failed.
  WHY: The PR cannot merge while the required check is red, and the cause is still unmapped. The full log for job 130823415856 is needed, plus a comparison against the merge base to tell a regression from an inherited failure. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash names one possible cause: the FakeGitHub PATCH-branch reorder in tests/test_operator_step_issue.py now matches any `state=open` PATCH. Severity disagreement: BLOCKER (gemini, luna) vs MAJOR (sonnet, glm); the highest is used.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:630-679 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `HUMAN_OBJECT_TITLE_RE` (lines 630-633) uses `\b...\b`, and `_` is a word character, so it never matches underscore-joined secret names such as `DEPLOY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN` or `API_KEY`. As a result, `_is_release_entry` (line 679) classifies a title-only step like "Sync DEPLOY_TOKEN to stable" as a release step.
  WHY: Once `compare/<sha>...stable` reports `ahead` or `identical`, `resolve()` auto-ticks the human step. If that was the last unticked step, it also closes the `ai:operator-step` tracker, even though the secret was never set. The regression test `test_operator_step_title_only_step_naming_a_secret_is_a_human_step` only covers titles that contain the word "secret". Severity disagreement: BLOCKER (minimax) vs MAJOR (sonnet, luna, glm); the highest is used.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:615 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `\b` word boundaries in the HUMAN_OBJECT_TITLE_RE regex do not match when the keyword directly follows an underscore (for example, DEPLOY_TOKEN).
  WHY: Steps like "Sync the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret..." are wrongly treated as automated release steps and auto-ticked, so they resolve while the human action is still undone. This is kept separate from the finding above because the cited line 615 is not within 5 lines of 630-679.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:758-830 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `operator_step_issue.py upsert` exits 3, lines 758-765 only set `activation_operator_unconfirmed="true"`. If the verdict-comment POST then also fails, the function returns at lines 812-815, before the only Telegram WARNING send at lines 825-827/825-830.
  WHY: Both failures come from the same GitHub API degradation, so they tend to happen together. When they do, the unconfirmed operator-step tracker produces only `::warning::` lines and no Telegram alert, which breaks the README/changelog promise that activation verification "sends a WARNING". Severity disagreement: MAJOR (sonnet, minimax, glm) vs NIT (luna); the highest is used.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:822-861 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `resolve()`, the fresh check in `_tracker_still_closable` (a GET at line 822) and the close PATCH (line 836) are separate calls with no conditional guard between them. The post-close check (lines 846-861/858-861) re-reads only entry comments, not the issue state.
  WHY: If a person reopens the tracker between the GET and the PATCH, the `state=closed` PATCH silently overwrites the reopen, which defeats the rule "never close a tracker a person reopened". `test_operator_step_resolve_keeps_a_tracker_reopened_during_the_tick_open` only covers a reopen that happens before the GET. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (gemini, minimax) vs NIT (glm); the highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 instead judged this window to be the documented residual of the close race ("narrows the close race; it does not make it atomic") and reported it as NONE.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:733-739,822-825,862 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_tracker_still_closable()` returns False both when the tracker was reopened and when a person closed it during the tick, but `resolve()` maps both to `reason = "reopened"` and logs `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE op=close issue=<n> outcome=open reason=reopened`.
  WHY: `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE` is a contractual log prefix (agents.d/stuck-states-p10-operator-step-resolve.md), so log analysis records the wrong outcome and reason for a tracker that is actually closed. The decision not to close is still safe. All reviewers rated this NIT.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:630-633, used at line 679 in `_is_release_entry` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `HUMAN_OBJECT_TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:secrets?|tokens?|credentials?|passwords?|variables?|settings?|permissions?|accounts?|keys?)\b", re.I)` does not split on `_`, so it misses `DEPLOY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN` and `API_KEY`. Titles like "Sync NPM_TOKEN to stable" or "Publish API_KEY to the stable environment", with no `dormant_until`, make `_is_release_entry` return True. The new test `test_operator_step_title_only_step_naming_a_secret_is_a_human_step` passes only because its title contains the word "secret".
  WHY: The step is written as a `pr-<n>` entry with a source SHA. Once `compare/<sha>...stable` reports `ahead` or `identical`, `resolve()` ticks it, and if it was the last unticked step it auto-closes the `ai:operator-step` tracker. The secret is never set and no person sees the step. Suggested fix: replace `\b` with the lookarounds `(?<![A-Za-z])`/`(?![A-Za-z])` and add a test titled "Sync NPM_TOKEN to stable".
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:`_tracker_still_closable` / `resolve()` close logging | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A tracker that a person closed during the tick is logged as `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE op=close issue=<n> outcome=open reason=reopened`.
  WHY: `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE` is a contractual log prefix (agents.d/stuck-states-p10-operator-step-resolve.md), so log analysis records the wrong outcome. The decision itself is safe. Suggested fix: return the fresh state and log `outcome=closed reason=closed_meanwhile`, and add that reason to the agents fragment (about 6 lines).
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:758-765, 812-815, 825-827 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: After an exit 3 from `upsert`, a failed verdict-comment POST makes the function return at line 815, before the WARNING at 825-827. Before the last run, the non-zero branch sent the WARNING immediately (line 769).
  WHY: These failures tend to happen together during a GitHub API degradation. When they do, the operator-step entry may sit on a closed tracker and the only signal is two `::warning::` lines, which contradicts the README and changelog. Suggested fix: send the WARNING before `return 0` when `activation_operator_unconfirmed` is true (about 3 lines).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:543 (job `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`); aggregate `lint` at line 3466 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The required check failed on head 66fe05bf631890d9b00ee2c2af9af527272ad551 and could not be mapped to a code site. The PR's own tests run at line 2391 in `tests-release-and-log-analysis` (lines 2131-2496), which passed. The log tail ends in the passing `tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` step.
  WHY: The PR cannot merge while `lint` is red. The full log for job 130823415856 and a comparison with the merge base are needed. From the available evidence, the PR's changed files are not exercised by this job.
- Concurrency: NONE. The GET→PATCH gap is the documented residual of the close race. Naming, implicit-execution and task-completeness: NONE. All #9203/P10 deliverables are present.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 630-632; 678-679 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `HUMAN_OBJECT_TITLE_RE` uses `\b(?:tokens?|...)\b`, so it does not match SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE names like `DEPLOY_TOKEN`. "Sync DEPLOY_TOKEN to stable" matches `RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE`, and `_is_release_entry` returns True.
  WHY: `resolve` ticks the step once `stable` contains the SHA and may close the tracker without the secret being set. This breaks the promise made in the CHANGELOG, agents fragment and README. The test only exercises the word "secret" (`tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:1109`). Suggested fix: `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(?:secrets?|...|keys?)(?![A-Za-z0-9])`, about 3 lines.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 822-836; post-close check at 858-861 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `_tracker_still_closable` GET (line 822) and the close PATCH (line 836) are separate calls. The post-close recheck compares only entry-comment IDs and does not re-read the issue state.
  WHY: A reopen that happens between the GET and the PATCH is silently overwritten. `test_operator_step_resolve_keeps_a_tracker_reopened_during_the_tick_open` only simulates a reopen before the GET.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:lines 758-765, 812-815, 825-830 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: On exit 3, the script sets `activation_operator_unconfirmed="true"` (line 765) and emits a `::warning::` plus an `activation_log` line (763-764). The Telegram WARNING comes after the verdict POST, so a failed POST (line 781) makes the function return at line 815 without sending it.
  WHY: During a GitHub API degradation the Telegram channel stays silent, which breaks the WARNING promised in the CHANGELOG, README and the comment at lines 759-762. Suggested fix: send the WARNING before `return 0` at line 815, about 5 lines.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 822-825, 862 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `resolve()` maps both "reopened" and "closed by a person" to `reason = "reopened"` and logs `outcome="open" reason="reopened"`.
  WHY: This misclassifies the event under the stable log prefix `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE op=close`. There is no runtime correctness impact.
- Concurrency: NONE (covered under Correctness). Implic
